definition: <mi>, person, with <kang>, white: a white person, also said of the British who ruled Burma; {mikang pau} is the English language and {mikang gam} the West

<mikang>, white person, and <kumpi>, king or government: the British colonial government that ruled Burma and the Zo hills, in accounts of history; with <te> for its officials and <khutnuai> for being under its rule
<mikang> and <gam> written as one word: the land of the white people, Europe and the West
<mikang>, white person, and <lai>, writing, written as one word: English as a written language and a subject of study
the English language as it is written: <mikang>, white person, with <lai>, writing; {Mikanglai in gelh} is write in English
<mikang>, Westerner, with <lai>, writing, and the plural <te>: English writings, English as a school subject
the English language, the speech, <pau>, of white people, <mikang>; often written with a capital
<mikang>, white person, with the plural <te>: white people, Westerners

terms: that of the English/the English one
definition: <mikangte>, the English, with <a> after it for the owner: theirs, the one of the English, here their grammar
<mikangte>, white people, and the subject marker <in> written as one word: the white people, as the ones who act
name of several men, and of the chief angel who fights for Israel
younger daughter of King Saul and wife of David
<mi>, person, and <khangto>, be developed, written as one word: people who are advanced in education and way of life
<mi>, person, with <khat>, one, written as one word: someone, anyone; with <suak> or <ahi> it means one people, one and the same

terms: only one person/one person alone/a single person
definition: <mikhat>, one person, and <bek>, only, written as one word: one person and no more, or one person acting alone
<mikhat>, someone, with the subject marker <in>, written as one word: someone as the doer of the action; also by one person, per person
<mikhat>, one person, and <liam>, be injured, written as one word: one person was hurt
<mikhat>, one person, with the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: one person, as the one spoken about; also each person
<mikhat>, someone, and <peuh>, any, written as one word: anyone at all, any one person
<mikhat> and <tek>, each, written as one word: each single person
<mikhat>, one person, with <zong>, also, written as one word: one person as well, most often {adang mikhatzong}, one other person too
<mi>, person, with <kheem>, deceive, and the plural <te>: deceivers, impostors
<mi> person with <khem> deceive; {mikhem theite} and {mikhem hatte} are deceivers, the treacherous
<mi>, people, and <khemkhem>, keep deceiving, written as one word: one who goes on deceiving people, or the deceiving of people
<mi>, person, with <khempa>, deceiver, written as one word: a man who deceives people
<mi> person with <khempeuh> all, written as one word; usually written {mi khempeuh}
<mikhem> deceive people, with plural <te>: those who deceive
<mi> person with <khial> go wrong and the plural <te>; in the verse the people the psalmist does not sit with, the deceitful in the NIV
<mi>, person, with <khual>, guest: a person from elsewhere who stays among others, often paired with <peemta>
<mikhual> stranger with the intensifying <pi>
plural of <mikhual>: foreigners who live among another people, paired with <peemtate>

terms: other people's hands/the hands of others
definition: <mi>, other people, and <khut>, hand, written as one word: the power or control of others; {mikhut sung} is in the hands of others and {mikhut nuai} under someone else, as an employee
<mi>, other people, and <khutnuai>, under the hand, written as one word: under the hand or rule of others; {mikhutnuai ah nasem} is work for someone else
<mi>, other people, and <kiang>, presence, written as one word, used as {mikiang ah}: at other people's side, with or before others, also at another person's place for work or food
<mi> person with <kician> sound, reliable; in the verse of several men
<mi>, person, with <kihisak>, be proud, written as one word: a person who thinks much of himself
<mikihisak>, a proud person, with the plural <te>
<mi>, person, with <kim>, every: each person, everyone; {mikim tungah} is to each one
<mikim> and the marker <in> written as one word: everyone, each person, as the one who acts
<mi> and <kitawng> written as one word: people fighting or quarrelling with one another, a brawl
Benjamite of Gibeon, father of Shimeah, in the family line of King Saul
town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem, also written <Mikmash>
town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem, where Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at the pass
placed after a verb: the thing simply happens or is done, mostly something unwelcome or undeserved, as in {thuak mikmek}, just have to suffer it; exact shade not determined
place east of Shechem on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh
Levite gatekeeper who played the harp when David brought the ark to Jerusalem
make fun of people or call them names, said of what is done to <mi>, other people; {miko mitotna} is mocking and provoking people
town in the south of Judah settled again after the exile
Benjamite, ancestor of Elah who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
an ant; {miksi hon khat} is a swarm of ants
plural of <miksi>, ant
<mi>, people, with <lak>, midst, written as one word: the company of other people; {milak ah} is in public, among people
musician in the procession at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem under Nehemiah
<mi>, person, and <lamdang>, astonishing, written as one word: a person who is strange or out of the ordinary
city in the north of Italy; also in the names of its football clubs AC Milan and Inter Milan
<mi>, person, and <lawhcing>, succeed, written as one word: a person who has succeeded
the measure of distance, about 1.6 kilometres
used only as the second half of the pair <migam milei>, the land of other people: a foreign country, a place that is not one's own
a numbered mile marker along a road, used to name places on the road by their distance
port city on the west coast of Asia Minor, where Paul met the elders of the church of Ephesus
<mi>, person, with <lian>, great: a person of high standing or power, the opposite of <mineu>
<milian> great person with the marker <in>, here as or into: made them great
<milian>, great person, with the intensive <pi>: a very great person, somebody of importance
plural of <milian>: great or high-ranking people, nobles
<miliante> written with a capital at the start of a sentence
<mi>, person, with <lim>, likeness: an image made to be worshipped, an idol; <milim biakna> is idolatry
a picture or likeness of a person or thing, with no thought of worship
<milim>, an image or idol, and <biakna>, worship: the worship of idols, idolatry

<milim>, idol, and <biate>, worshippers: those who worship idols. In church writing it also names the people of other religions as a group, in contrast to Christians; the word before it names the country or place they belong to
<milim>, idol, and <bia>, worship, written as one word: one who worships idols
<milim> idol, image with the marker <in>; {milimin bawl} is make something into an idol
plural of <milim>: idols, images made to be worshipped
<milim>, picture, with the plural <te>
each person individually, usually as {a milip-in}, each of them
all the people of a country or place taken as a number, where the other sense is each one separately; <milip simna> or {milip kisimna} is a census
<milip>, population, and <simna>, counting or reading: the official counting of the people of a country, a census; {gambup milip simna} is the national census, often after the year
person by person, counting or assessing each individual; used with <a> before it, {a milipin}
<milip> everyone with the plural ending <un>; usually {a milipun}, each and every one of them
member of an armed extremist group; often written beside <migilo>, evildoer
members of an armed group that fights a government; taken over with the English plural ending and used for one or many
armed group of civilians, in Myanmar news mostly one that fights on the side of the army
wife of Nahor, the brother of Abraham, and grandmother of Rebekah; also one of the five daughters of Zelophehad
god of the Ammonites, called Molek in the NIV
the number one million, written before or after the figure it counts
the English plural used as the number word million, written after the number or before it
part of the defences of the City of David in Jerusalem, built up by David and Solomon; the NIV has the terraces, and Beth Millo for {Millo inn}
after <moi> young, tender: {a moi milmel}, delicately tender
placed after <om> be, or after <hai> or {lung am sak}: staying dull, dazed and unresponsive, without speaking or showing feeling, not the tender of {moi milmel}
not clear or bright: of seeing, dimly; after a colour word, dull, as {a kang milmial}, dull white
<mi>, person, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not a person of, one who does not belong to; {Pasian milo} is not one of God's people
<mi>, person, with <lom>, batch: a number of people taken together, as against one alone
<mi>, person, and <luang>, body, written as one word: the body of a person, here a person taken for a debt
<mi>, person, and <lui>, old, written as one word: someone of the old kind, as the old self before faith, or those who have long been in a group or in office, set against <mithak>, the new
<mi>, person, and <lungsim>, heart or mind, written as one word: the mind or heart of people; {milungsim zo} is win people over
city in the state of Wisconsin in the United States
a grain crop, millet or Job's tears, compare <vaimim>, maize; in songs paired with {sawmtang} for the grain one lives on, and {mim bang piang} is a phrase of songs for being born into this world
<mi> person with the emphatic <mah>: himself a man, truly human
<mi>, people, with <mai>, face or front, written as one word: before other people, in public, mostly as {mimai ah}
<mi> person with <mal> single unit: individual persons; in the verse the number of members that grows
placed before a noun: belonging to one person and not to a group or the public, as <mimal vai>, a personal matter, and <mimal muhna>, a personal view
grammar term: a pronoun that stands for a person or thing, as <kei>, <nang>, <amah>; divided into <mi masa>, <mi nihna> and <mi thumna>

<mimal>, individual, and <muhdan>, view: one person's own view of a matter, not that of an organization; common in the titles of opinion pieces, the subject before it and the name of the writer after it

terms: personal opinion/personal view/own point of view
definition: <mimal>, individual, and <muhna>, way of seeing: the opinion of one person and not of a group; writers mark an article with {mimal muhna pan}, from a personal point of view, and say {kei mimal muhna}, my personal opinion
<mimal>, individual person, and <phazah>, number: the number of persons counted one by one, the headcount of a group or the population of a place

<mimal>, an individual, and <tangdin>, standing alone: a candidate or member of parliament who belongs to no party, named beside those who stand for a party; also placed after a name in a list of candidates
<mimal>, an individual, and <vai>, here a matter or affair: a matter that concerns one person only, a private or personal affair, privacy; set against the affairs of a group or the public
<mimal>, individual, with <in>, written as one word: as an individual or as individuals; {kei mimalin} is I personally
<mimal> individual and <kim> every written as one word: each single person

<mimal>, personal, and <mintaang>, pronoun, written as one word: the grammar term for the personal pronoun; the table of the book lists under it the forms {kei'}, {nang'}, {ei'}, {amau'}, me, you, us, them
<mimal>, individual, with the plural <te>: single persons, as against a group, a church or an organisation
<mimal>, individual, and <vai>, affair, written as one word: what concerns one person only, set against the affairs of the people or the country
<mi>, person, and <man>, seize, written as one word: catch or carry off people, as kidnappers do; also of the disciples as fishers of men
<mi>, person, with <mang>, here be lost: someone who has disappeared and is being looked for
<mi>, person, and <mangcip>, disappear, written as one word: a person who has gone missing, as after a disaster
<mi>, person, and <masa>, first, written as one word: the first or earliest person or people, as Adam the first man; before <makaite>, the earlier leaders
<mi> and <masate> written as one word: the people who came or led before, the earlier leaders
<mi> person with <mat> seize: a person taken; {galte’ mimat}, captive of the enemy
<mi>, person, with <mawh>, sin: a sinner, a guilty person; {mimawh lo} is an innocent person
plain, unlearned people of low standing, named beside <mihai>, the foolish, and glossed as grassroots people by one writer; not the sinner of the other sense
plural of <mimawh>: sinners, guilty people, often set against <midikte>, the righteous
<mi>, person, with <mawkmawk>, ordinary, written as one word: a person of no special rank or standing
<mi>, person, with <mawl>, dull: a senseless person, paired with <mihai>, fool
<mi>, person, and <mel>, appearance, written as one word: the face or looks of a person, the form of a human being

terms: man by man/person by person/one by one
definition: <mi> person doubled, with <in>: each person in turn, like {a behbehin} clan by clan and {a innkuankuanin} family by family
<mi> and <min> written as one word: a person's name; {mimin thang} is a famous person, more often written {mi minthang}
a thread, a thin strand of spun fibre used for weaving and sewing
one grain of <mim>, millet, and one grain of <taang.2>, a grain crop, said as a pair: a single tiny grain, the smallest thing that could be shared
<mi>, person, with <muan>, trust: a person someone relies on, a trusted helper or adviser of a leader
<mi>, people, and <muhna>, sight, written as one word: where people can see; {mimuhna ah} is in public, in front of people
in grammar, the word class that names people, animals, places and things
of fruit, to be ripe; {min dektak} is almost ripe
<min>, name, written with a capital for the name of God, as in {Min Siangtho}, the holy Name, and at the start of a sentence

<min>, name, and <kitaih>, collide: a clash of names, said of refugee resettlement files held back because the name or identity of the applicant conflicts with another record, a fraud case; {min kitaih te} are the persons whose files are so held

terms: be named/be called/be given the name
definition: <min>, name, and <kivawh>, be given: to be given a name; the name stands before it, followed by <cih> or <ci'n>, and {min kivawh lampi} is the road so named
a unit of weight for silver and gold, sixty shekels in Ezekiel 45:12
<min>, name, written together with <a>, a short form of <ah>, in: in the name of, as in {Topa' mina}, in the name of the Lord; not the unit of weight
a people of one descent and language

<minam.3>, a people or race, and <deidan>, treat unequally: unequal treatment of people because of their race or tribe; used as a noun with <nei>, have, <thuak>, suffer, or <piang>, arise, and also as a verb, discriminate by race
<minam>, a people, and <hihna>, the fact of being: the fact of being a people or of belonging to one, its identity; a possessive such as <i> or <a> stands before it

<minam>, people or nation, and <it>, love: love one's own people, be devoted to the nation; the object stands before the verb without a marker, and the pair also stands before a noun, as in {minam it zia}, the way of loving one's people
<minam>, a people or nation, and <itna>, love: love of one's own people, the feeling that moves a person to work for the nation

<minam>, a people, and <khangto>, grow: a people that has advanced in learning and prosperity, a developed nation, said beside {gam khangto}, a developed country; the same two words also form a clause, a people advances

terms: established nation/recognised people/people in its own right
definition: <minam>, a people or nation, and <kician>, firm, well-founded: a people that stands as a full nation in its own right, with its own name, language and recognition; often with <khat> after it and a people's name before it, {Zomi minam kician khat}
<minam.3>, a people or nation, and <kipumkhatna>, unity: the oneness of a people across its clans, dialects and churches, a set term of Zomi public life

terms: ethnic/bearing the name of the people/national
definition: <minam>, a people, and <minpua>, bearing the name of: placed before <party> or <kipawlna>, a party or body that carries the name of an ethnic group and stands for it
<minam>, a people or ethnic group, and <party>, political party: a political party that stands for one ethnic group, as against a party of the whole country; a term of the politics of Myanmar
<minam>, people or nation, and <puan>, cloth: the woven cloth or dress that marks a people, worn at festivals; {Zo minam puan} is the Zo national dress, set against {fashion puan}
<minam> nation with <bup> whole
a people or ethnic group other than one’s own, also one living in the same country, as the non-Zomi peoples of Myanmar; not only a foreigner from abroad
<minamdang> foreigner, another people, with plural <te>
<minam>, nation, with the marker <in>: as a nation, into a nation, nation by nation; {minamin bawl} is make into a nation
one of the branches into which a people, <minam>, divides; paired with {pauke}, a branch of a language
<minam> people with {kee}, branch: one of the smaller groups into which a people is divided, each often with its own speech
<minam>, people, and <khat>, one, written as one word: a people or nation, one people
<minam>, a people, and <kim.2>, every, written as one word: peoples of every kind, all the ethnic groups
<minam> and <lian> written as one word: a great or powerful nation
<minam>, nation, and <ni>, day, written as one word: the day a people keeps as its national day, as the Zomi National Day
<minam>, a people, with <pi>, great: a large or leading people or nation
<minam>, people or tribe, with <pih>, fellow: a person of the same people as oneself
plural of <minampi>: the large or leading peoples and nations
plural of <minam>: the nations or peoples of the world
plural of <minam> used for the tribes of Israel
capitalised form of <minamte> placed after a tribal name in the land allotments of Ezekiel 48, as in {Asher Minamte} the tribe of Asher
<minam>, a people, and <vai>, affair, written as one word: the affairs and cause of one's own people, often paired as {gamvai minamvai}, the affairs of the land and of the people
unit of weight for gold and silver, written as in English
<mi> and <nautang> written as one word: the ordinary people, civilians as distinct from soldiers, police and officials
{mi nautang}, common people, with the plural <te>; {minautangte’ tutna mun}, the seat of the common people, is the lowest place at a feast
be cooked or done, with <baih>, soon: of food, become cooked or tender in a short time
town and district on the Irrawaddy in Magway Region of Myanmar
a town in Rakhine State in Myanmar
earth that slides down a slope, mostly after heavy rain; the second part is <cim>, collapse
lose one's good name, be shamed before others; often {mindai-in} together with <maizum>, be ashamed
loss of one's good name; {mindai ni} is a day of disgrace
<mindai>, be disgraced, with <huai>, deserving of: shameful, said of detestable conduct
<mindaihuai>, shameful, with the plural <te>: shameful or detestable deeds
<mindai>, be disgraced, with the noun suffix <na>: the loss of one's good name; {mindaina tun} is to bring dishonor on someone
plural of <mindaina>: the disgraces a people has suffered or brought on itself
<mindaina>, disgrace, with <teng>, all: the whole of one's disgrace
<mindai>, be disgraced, with the causative <sak>: bring shame or dishonor on someone
<mindaisak>, put to shame, with the noun suffix <na>: the scorn or insults by which others shame someone
the large island and region in the south of the Philippines
<min>, name, with <dang>, other: a second name of a person, or a name other than the one just mentioned
a town and township in the south of Chin State, Myanmar, and its people
<min>, name, and <deih.2>, want, written as one word: wish to be well known or to have a title
<min>, name, and <ding>, to be, written as one word: the name that something is to have, as its name
an explosive laid in or on the ground; {mine siah} is lay a mine and {mine sikkha} is step on a mine
<mi>, person, with <neu>, small: a person of low standing, usually paired with <milian>, the great
<mineu> lowly person with the superlative <pen>
plural of <mineu>, people of low standing, the opposite of <miliante>
a township in the north of Yangon
a township in the north of <Yangon>
<mi>, person, with <ngau.2>, destitute; said in a pair with <mizawng>, the poor and needy, over against <mihau>, the rich
<mi>, person, with <ngongtat>, be violent: one who uses violence, a thug, robber or terrorist
Burmese title of a high official, placed after what he is in charge of: {Lam Mingyi} is the chief officer for roads
<min>, name, with <hoih>, good: a good name, either a good reputation or a fine personal name
<mi>, person, with <niam>, low: a person of low position; {miniam i hih laitak} is when we were lowly
<miniam>, lowly person, written with a capital at the start of a verse; {Miniam ihih laitakin} is when we were lowly
name of several men, among them a Levite under King Hezekiah and a priest in the time of Nehemiah
plural of <miniam>: people of low position or humble spirit, whom God lifts up
a small bus
<mi> person with <nih> two, written as one word

terms: the two people/the two men/both of them
definition: <minih>, two people, with the plural <te>: the two persons spoken of
<min>, name, with the marker <in>: by name or in the name of someone; also as subject, the name is
<mi>, person, with <nin>, unclean, and the plural <te>; paired with <misiangte>, the clean
a member of a government who heads a ministry; {Prime Minister} is the head of the government; also used of a minister of a church
one of the sixty parts of an hour, a loanword from English
a name borne in place of the real one; in the verse the city is figuratively called Sodom and Egypt
<min>, name, with <khumna>, putting in: the entering of a name in a list, as registration with the UNHCR; also the list itself
<min>, name, with <kip>, firm: a name written on a document to confirm it; {minkip gelh} is to sign
<min>, name, with <lawh>, call, and the noun ending {-na}: the name by which a thing is called; the heading of a list of special names for animals and relatives
<min>, name, <le>, and, and <za>, rank, written as one word: the name and standing a person has among others
<min>, name, with <lian>, great: having a great name, exalted
the noun, a great name that a person or a people has or gains, named beside <minhoih>, a good name, and as the object of <neih>, have; not said of the one who is renowned
form of <minlian> used before <nading>: {na minliat nading}, your being honoured
<minliat>, be great in name, with the noun suffix <na>: majesty, the greatness and honour of a king or of God
not cooked through, said of meat; the first part is the verb for be ripe or be cooked, with <lo>, not
<min>, name, and <mai>, front, written as one word: the place before a personal name, where a title such as {Siapi}, <Major> or <Tang> is put; such a title takes no full stop

terms: word of a name/part of a name
definition: <min>, name, with <mal>, single unit: one of the words that make up a personal name, as {Hau}, {Cin} and {Khup} in Hau Cin Khup

terms: words of a name/parts of a name
definition: <minmal> with the plural <te>: the separate words of a personal name
<min> ripe, doubled: beginning to ripen, said of figs
city in the state of Minnesota in the United States
<min>, name, with <nei>, have: bearing the name, placed after a personal name
<minnei>, bearing the name, with <khat>, one, written as one word and placed after a personal name, often after <kici>: a person of that name
a state in the north of the United States of <America>
<min>, name, with <neu>, small: a short or familiar name beside the full name, <minpi>
kingdom summoned with Ararat and Ashkenaz to make war on Babylon
place east of the Jordan, as far as which Jephthah struck down the Ammonites
<min>, name, with <no>, small: a second name by which a person is known
the smaller group within a population, mostly of peoples and religions, as in {Ethnic Minority}; the opposite is majority
<min> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the name of the person or thing just mentioned, as for the name
<min>, name, with <pha>, good: a good name, a good reputation
<min>, name, with <phat>, praise: praise the name of someone; {minphat ding}, to be praised, is set against {minsiat ding}, to be disgraced
<minphat>, praise, with <huai>, worthy of: deserving praise, well thought of
being well spoken of, the opposite of <mindaina>
plural of <minphatna>: the honors given to a person
<min>, name, and <phuah>, make up, written as one word: give a name to something, with the name before <ci-in>
<min> and <phuak> written as one word: give a name to a place, a person or a thing
<min>, name, with <pi>, great: the real, formal name of a person, set against {min neu}, the pet name or short name
<min>, name, and <pia>, give, written as one word: give a name to something
<min>, name, and <pia>, give, written as one word: hand in the name, register for an examination or apply for work

terms: bearing the name of/named after/in name
definition: <min>, name, and <pua>, carry, written as one word and placed after a name: bearing that name, representing it, or having it in name only

terms: those bearing the name/bearers of the name
definition: <minpua> with the plural <te>: the people who bear the name given before it, as {Zo minpuate}, those called Zo
town and township in Rakhine State in the west of Myanmar
of meat or food, already cooked: <min>, cooked or ripe, with <sa>, already; the opposite of <sial>, raw
<min>, name, with <sazian>, list: a written list of the names of people, as for joining, registering or receiving help
follows the name that something carries: {Zomi minsel party} is a party that bears the Zomi name
the name by which a parent is called after a child, the name of the child followed by <pa> or <nu>, as {Lianpu pa}, father of Lianpu, and {Lam Vung nu}, mother of Lam Vung
<min>, name, with <sia>, bad; {minsia tun} is to bring a bad name on someone and {minsia sak} is to disgrace
call out one's own name and deeds in the traditional manner of men, as a boast, a challenge or a strong vow
<minsia>, bad name, with the causative <sak>: give someone a bad name, bring disgrace on someone
form of <minsia>, bad name, used as a verb before <ding>: get a bad name; set against <minphat>, be praised
<minsia>, bad name, with <tham>, worth: enough to bring a bad name, deserving disgrace

terms: be disgraced by/get a bad name through
definition: <minsiat> and <lawh.2> written as one word: get a bad name as the outcome of something done
the spoiling of one's name, loss of good reputation
<min>, name, and <suang> written as one word after the name: bearing that name, in the name of
<min>, ripe, with <ta>, now: has become ripe, said of fruit ready for harvest
grammar term: any word used in the place of a name or noun, from <min>, name, with <taang>, stand in place of; the book gives <amah>, <nangma>, <keimah> and counts five kinds
<min>, name, and <taanga>, in place of, written as one word: instead of the name or noun; the thought behind the grammar term <mintaang>, pronoun
of cooking, until the food is fully cooked, followed by <in> or <a>; the first part is the word for cooked or ripe that is found in <minsa>
<min>, name, and <taktak>, real, written as one word
known by name to many people, as in {mi mintang}, a famous person; probably another spelling of <minthang>
<min>, name, with <tap>, name after: a name taken over from an elder in the Zomi way of naming, or the person who bears it

terms: in the name of/under the name of/by name
